\begin{lemma}[Combined point measurements]
	\label{lem:qld-4-10}
	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.CombinedPointsWitness}
	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_combinedPointsWitness}
	\notready
	\uses{def:expanded-state, def:expanded-point-measurement,
		def:povm-distance, def:symmetric-equivalents}
	There exists a function $\delta_Q(\eps) = \poly(\eps)$ such that the
	following holds. For every $x, z \in \F_q^m$ and
	$\hilb \in \{\hilb_{\mathsf{A}}, \hilb_{\mathsf{B}}\}$ there are
	projective measurements $\{\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}\}_{a,b \in \F_q}$ acting
	on $\hilb \ot (\C^q)^{\ot M}$ such that:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item (\textbf{Self-consistency}) On average over uniformly random
		$x, z \in \F_q^m$,
		\begin{equation}
			\label{eq:qld-q-self-cons}
			(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
			\approx_{\delta_Q}
			(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}\,.
		\end{equation}
		\item (\textbf{Consistency with $\hat{M}$}) On average over uniformly
		random $x, z \in \F_q^m$,
		\begin{gather}
			\label{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-xz}
			(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
			\approx_{\delta_Q}
			(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}_{a} \,
			\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_{b})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}\,,
			\\
			\label{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-zx}
			(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
			\approx_{\delta_Q}
			(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_{b} \,
			\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}_{a})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}\,.
		\end{gather}
	\end{enumerate}
	Furthermore, all symmetric equivalents of these approximations also hold.
	The operators $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}_{a}$ and
	$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_{b}$ do not commute in general, so the
	products in \eqref{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-xz} and
	\eqref{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-zx} differ and the two relations are separate
	conclusions.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
	\uses{lem:qld-comm-cons, def:expanded-point-trace-projection,
		fact:add-a-proj, fact:agreement, lem:ortho, thm:linearity,
		lem:avg-closeness, lem:cancellation, def:povm-distance}
	Throughout the proof every intermediate error is a $\poly(\eps)$ function
	that may differ from one use of $\approx_\delta$ to the next. For
	$\omega = (x,z,r,s) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q^m \times \F_q \times \F_q$
	and $a, b \in \F_2$ define the sandwich POVM
	$\hat{R}^{\omega}_{a,b}
	= \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z,s}_{b}
	\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x,r}_{a}
	\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z,s}_{b}$
	from the binary refinements of
	Definition~\ref{def:expanded-point-trace-projection}; by the approximate
	commutation of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-comm-cons}, projectivity, and
	Lemma~\ref{fact:add-a-proj}, on average over $\omega$ one has
	$\hat{R}^{\omega}_{a,b}
	\approx_{\sqrt{\delta_{\mathrm{acom}}}}
	\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z,s}_{b}
	\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x,r}_{a}$,
	and a Cauchy--Schwarz chain with successive errors
	$\delta_{\mathrm{acom}}^{1/4}$, $\delta_{\mathrm{acom}}^{1/4}$,
	$\sqrt{\eps}$, $\eps$ establishes the self-consistency
	$(\hat{R}^{\omega}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \simeq_\delta
	(\hat{R}^{\omega}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}$, hence the
	corresponding $\approx_\delta$ relation by Lemma~\ref{fact:agreement}.
	The orthonormalization lemma (Lemma~\ref{lem:ortho}) then produces
	projective measurements $\{\hat{L}^{\omega}_{a,b}\}$ with
	$\hat{L}^{\omega}_{a,b} \approx_\delta \hat{R}^{\omega}_{a,b}$ on
	average over $\omega$. Next, the refined point measurements satisfy the
	exact linearity
	$\sum_{b+b'=c} \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u,r}_{b}
	\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u,r'}_{b'}
	= \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u,r+r'}_{c}$
	(a direct consequence of projectivity of
	$\{\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a\}$), which transfers, on average over
	$x, z, r, r', s, s'$, to an approximate linearity of the
	$\{\hat{R}^{\omega}_{a,b}\}$ in the index pair $(r,s)$ and then to the
	$\{\hat{L}^{\omega}_{a,b}\}$. Consequently the binary observables
	$\mathcal{O}^{\omega}
	= \sum_{a,b \in \F_2} (-1)^{a+b} \hat{L}^{\omega}_{a,b}$
	satisfy
	$\mathcal{O}^{x,z,r,s} \mathcal{O}^{x,z,r',s'}
	\approx_\delta \mathcal{O}^{x,z,r+r',s+s'}$
	on average over $x, z, r, r', s, s'$. Identify $\F_q \cong \F_2^t$ so
	that the pair $(r,s)$ ranges over $\F_2^{2t}$, and let $\rho$ be the
	reduced density operator of $\ket{\hat\psi}$ on the registers carrying
	the $\mathcal{O}^{\omega}$, so that $\Tr(S\rho)$ is the expectation
	value of $S$ in $\ket{\hat\psi}$ for every operator $S$ on those
	registers. For fixed $(x,z)$ let $\delta_{x,z}$ denote the
	conditional average, given $(x,z)$, of the squared linearity defect
	$\lVert (\mathcal{O}^{x,z,r,s} \mathcal{O}^{x,z,r',s'}
	- \mathcal{O}^{x,z,r+r',s+s'}) \ket{\hat\psi} \rVert^2$, so that
	$\E_{x,z}\, \delta_{x,z} = O(\delta)$; expanding the square, using
	unitarity of the observables, and relabelling the averaged index pair
	shows that, for each $(x,z)$, the correlation hypothesis of
	Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity} holds in the form
	$\E\, \Tr(\mathcal{O}^{x,z,r,s} \mathcal{O}^{x,z,r',s'}
	\mathcal{O}^{x,z,r+r',s+s'} \rho)
	= 1 - \tfrac{1}{2}\delta_{x,z}$,
	the average being over $(r,s)$ and $(r',s')$ uniform in $\F_2^{2t}$.
	Since Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity} imposes no upper bound on its error
	parameter, it applies for every fixed $(x,z)$ with
	$\delta := \tfrac{1}{2}\delta_{x,z}$ and yields binary observables
	$\{\mathcal{L}^{x,z,r,s}\}$, exactly linear in $(r,s)$ for all pairs,
	acting on an extension by an ancilla register in a pure state, with
	$\E_{r,s}\, d\big(\mathcal{L}^{x,z,r,s},\ \mathcal{O}^{x,z,r,s} \ot
	\Id\big)^2 \le \delta_{x,z}$
	in the state-dependent distance of the extended state; taking the
	expectation over $(x,z)$ shows that the two families are
	$\delta$-close, in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:povm-distance},
	on average over $x, z, r, s$, the averaged form of closeness being
	the one Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity} supplies and the only one used
	below (Remark~\ref{rem:linearity-import}).

	% and its pure state produced by thm:linearity may depend on (x,z);

	projection, and the family sums to the identity because
	$\sum_{a,b} \hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b} = \mathcal{L}^{x,z,0,0} = \Id$, the
	latter identity because exact linearity at $(r,s) = (r',s') = (0,0)$
	makes $\mathcal{L}^{x,z,0,0}$ an idempotent unitary; so
	$\{\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}\}$ is a
	projective measurement recovering $\F_q$-valued outcomes from the binary
	data by Fourier averaging over $(r,s)$. Its self-consistency
	\eqref{eq:qld-q-self-cons} follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:avg-closeness}
	together with the self-consistency of the $\{\mathcal{O}^{\omega}\}$;
	the consistency \eqref{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-zx} follows from a Fourier

	Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-comm-cons} into the same chain. Repeating the argument
	with the tensor factors on registers $\mathsf{B}\mathsf{B}'$ and
	$\mathsf{A}\mathsf{B}''$ gives all symmetric equivalents.

This makes the proof frontier visible without weakening the statement\nof a source-labelled theorem.\n\n### Why legacy scaffolding may remain temporarily\n\n| Temporary reason | Explanation |\n|------------------|-------------|\n| **Localizing an obstruction** | A conditional helper can isolate the exact missing mathematical input while the obligation discharger is being proved. |\n| **Recovering useful proof content** | The proof body may contain genuine estimates or constructions that should be extracted into source-faithful lemmas. |\n| **Auditability** | An explicit temporary hypothesis is easier to find than an implicit assumption hidden in prose, provided it is named as proof debt. |\n\nThese reasons do not justify strengthening a paper theorem.  They only explain\nwhy a short-lived helper declaration may exist while its remaining hypotheses\nare being actively removed.\n\n### How to proceed when a proof needs an extra input\n\n1. **Check the source statement.**  Read the corresponding TeX in\n   `references/ldt-paper/` before changing a theorem linked from the blueprint.\n2. **Keep the paper-facing declaration source-faithful.**  Boundary hypotheses\n   such as positivity, nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances, or\n   type-class assumptions may be faithful encodings when they are needed to\n   state the mathematics in Lean.  Proof data such as `BridgeInputs`,\n   `RepairInput`, `Residual`, `Package`, generic `Hypotheses`, or generic\n   `Assumptions` is different: it is not a paper assumption unless the cited\n   statement says so.\n3. **Name the missing intermediate result.**  If the proof uses a mathematical\n   fact not yet formalized, state it as a separate proof obligation.  A\n   temporary `sorry` in this declaration is preferable to adding the obligation as\n   a hypothesis on the paper theorem.\n4. **Do not introduce conditional helpers by default.**  A helper whose name\n   ends in `_ofObligations` is a quarantine device, not a normal formalization\n   pattern. If the helper would merely package missing work as an extra\n   hypothesis, restore the theorem with the paper statement and leave a tracked\n   `sorry` instead.\n5. **Audit the final statement.**  Every PR touching a source-labelled theorem\n   should compare paper assumptions and Lean assumptions, paper conclusion and\n   Lean conclusion, and report whether the Lean statement is exact, has only\n   faithful boundary hypotheses, or has extra assumptions.\n\nIf a paper-facing declaration is temporarily proved by calling a conditional\nhelper whose load-bearing input has not yet been produced from the paper\nhypotheses, the proof frontier must be marked explicitly.  The declaration\nshould carry an `**Unfaithful:**` docstring section naming the non-paper\ndependency, citing the paper-gap note or tracking issue, and identifying the\ninternal theorem that will remove the dependency.  A named proof obligation\nwith a tracked `sorry` is preferred whenever possible, because it makes the\nmissing mathematical assertion visible without adding it to the paper theorem\nstatement.\n\n### Required metadata for new proof-obligation declarations\n\nA new declaration whose name contains a proof-debt token such as `Bridge`,\n`Residual`, `Repair`, `Package`, `Producer`, `Input`, `Hypotheses`,\n`Assumptions`, `Obligation`, or `Witness` must explain its mathematical role in\nthe def-site docstring.  A paper citation alone is not enough, because the\nreviewer must be able to tell whether the declaration is part of the paper\nstatement or a Lean-only proof obligation.\n\nUse one of the following markers.\n\n| Marker | Use |\n|--------|-----|\n| `**Source:**`, `**Paper source:**`, or `**Source statement:**` | The declaration is a faithful formal encoding of a cited source statement or a field of that statement |\n| `**Faithful encoding:**` | The declaration records boundary data or domain data that the paper uses implicitly |\n| `**Proof obligation:**` or `**Internal proof obligation:**` | The declaration is a theorem or record that must be proved from the paper hypotheses before a source theorem is complete |\n| `**Conditional:**` | The declaration is a conditional helper; it must not be linked as the source theorem |\n| `**Unfaithful:**` | The declaration or proof currently depends on a load-bearing assumption not yet derived from the paper hypotheses |\n\nProof-obligation, conditional, and unfaithful markers must cite a paper-gap note\nor tracking issue and must state the planned discharge or elimination theorem.\nIf such a declaration would merely package missing work as an added hypothesis\nto a source theorem, do not introduce it; restore the source theorem statement\nand leave the missing proof as a tracked `sorry`.\n\n### Conditional helper boundary\n\n1. **Prefer a source theorem with a tracked `sorry`.**  If a proof requires a\n   construction that is not yet available from the paper hypotheses, the first\n   repair is to restore the source theorem statement and leave the missing proof\n   open. The earlier same-carrier auxiliary interface has\nbeen retired; the headline theorem carries no bridge, residual, repair,\npackage, producer, generic hypothesis, or proof-obligation input in its public\nstatement.\n\n### Distinction from anti-patterns\n\nThis rule addresses the same risk as conclusion-shaped-hypothesis smuggling\n(anti-pattern A1 in `docs/anti_patterns.md`), but it is stricter for\npaper-labelled declarations:\n\n- A conclusion-shaped hypothesis is always unacceptable.\n- A genuine intermediate fact may appear only in a separately named conditional\n  helper while its obligation discharger is being proved.\n- That same intermediate fact is still unacceptable as an added hypothesis on\n  the public statement of the paper theorem, unless it is a faithful encoding\n  of a hypothesis present in the cited source.\n\nObligation structures that bundle still-unproved theorem-level steps are proof\ndebt under this pattern. This is the error denoted $\\delta_S$ in Lemma~\\ref{lem:qld-4-7}; we call it $\\delta_G$ here to distinguish the global polynomial-pair witness error from the enlarged error used below. The remark below records the corrected statements.\n    57\t\\begin{remark}[Choice of decoding map and the decoder--encoder identity]\\label{rem:qld-decoding-identity}\n    58\t\tThe source states the constructions of this chapter in terms of its boolean decoding map (the case $H = \\{0,1\\}$ of Definition~\\ref{def:decoding-map}) while describing that map as returning the string of \\emph{all} evaluations of $g$ on the hypercube. The two usages occur in disjoint contexts.\n    98\t\\end{remark}\n    99\t\n   100\t\\begin{definition}[Symmetric games and symmetric strategies]\\label{def:symmetric-game}\n   101\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.SymmetricGame, MIPStarRE.QPBT.SymmetricGame.toGame, MIPStarRE.QPBT.SymmetricStrategy, MIPStarRE.QPBT.SymmetricStrategy.toStrategy}\n   102\t\t\\leanok\n   103\t\t% Paper label: rem:symmetric-games (a definition environment carrying a rem: label in the\n   104\t\t% source); relabeled here to match the environment kind.\n   105\t\t\\uses{def:game, def:tensor-product-strategy}\n   106\t\tA game $\\mathfrak G = (\\mathcal X, \\mathcal Y, \\mathcal A, \\mathcal B, \\mu, D)$ is \\emph{symmetric} if the question and answer alphabets are the same for both players (i.e.\\ $\\mathcal X = \\mathcal Y$ and $\\mathcal A = \\mathcal B$), the distribution $\\mu$ is symmetric (i.e.\\ $\\mu(x,y) = \\mu(y,x)$ for all $x,y$), and the decision predicate $D$ treats both players symmetrically (i.e.\\ $D(x,y,a,b) = D(y,x,b,a)$ for all $x,y,a,b$).\n   107\t\n   108\t\tA strategy $\\mathcal S = (\\ket{\\psi}, A, B)$ is \\emph{symmetric} if $\\ket{\\psi}$ is a (pure) state in $\\mathcal H \\ot \\mathcal H$, for some Hilbert space $\\mathcal H$, that is invariant under permutation of the two factors, and the measurement operators of both players are identical.\n   109\t\\end{definition}\n   110\t\n   111\tWe often specify symmetric games $\\mathfrak G$ and symmetric strategies $\\mathcal S$ using a compact notation: we write $\\mathfrak G = (\\mathcal X, \\mathcal A, \\mu, D)$ and $\\mathcal S = (\\ket{\\psi}, M)$, where $M$ denotes the set of measurement operators shared by both players.\n   112\t\n   113\t% Source statement (references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:94-99) kept in\n   114\t% its original form. It is meant for\ncontributors and reviewers who must decide whether a bridge, residual, repair,\ninput, or obligation structure is a proved local construction, a tracked proof\ngap, or statement drift which must be repaired before a theorem may be\nadvertised as a source theorem.  The default rule is restrictive: such data\nmust not be added to a paper-facing theorem unless it is part of the cited\nsource statement or a documented faithful encoding of its ambient hypotheses.\n\n\\section{Basic objects}\n\n\\paragraph{Source theorem.}\nA source theorem is a theorem, lemma, proposition, or corollary in the paper\nsource under \\path{references/ldt-paper/}.  Its hypotheses and conclusion are\nthe mathematical ground truth, subject only to faithful formal encoding and to\ndocumented paper-gap corrections.\n\n\\paragraph{Paper-facing declaration.}\nA \\Lean{} declaration is paper-facing when it is named or cited as the\nformalization of a source theorem, for instance through a blueprint\n\\verb|\\lean{}| link on a theorem environment carrying a paper label.  Such a\ndeclaration must match the source theorem in its public statement.  In\nparticular, it may not add an unproved bridge, residual, repair, input,\nobligation structure, or other proof-obligation hypothesis which the paper does\nnot assume.\n\n\\paragraph{Proof obligation.}\nA proof obligation is an intermediate assertion needed by the proof of a source\ntheorem.  It may be a construction, an estimate, a transport lemma, or a\ncomparison between two formal representations.  If the paper proves or invokes\nthis assertion, then the formalization should state it as a separate lemma or\ntheorem and prove it from the upstream hypotheses.\n\n\\paragraph{Obligation discharger.}\nAn obligation discharger is a theorem or definition which constructs a proof\nobligation from the paper hypotheses already available at that point in the\nargument.  This is the preferred representation of missing work.  If the proof\nis not yet complete, the discharger may temporarily contain a tracked\n\\verb|sorry|, but the paper-facing theorem should call it rather than assume\nits output as an additional theorem hypothesis.\n\n\\paragraph{Conditional helper.}\nA conditional helper is a separately named theorem whose statement explicitly\nassumes a proof obligation.  Names such as\n\\leanid{mainFormal\\_ofInternalObligations},\n\\leanid{orthonormalization\\_ofInput}, or names whose suffix advertises the\nassumed obligation are permitted only when the declaration is not presented as\nthe source theorem.  A conditional helper is a quarantine for downstream proof\ncontent; it does not close the source theorem.\n\n\\section{Bridge, residual, repair, input, and obligation structures}\n\nThe words \\emph{bridge}, \\emph{residual}, \\emph{repair}, \\emph{input}, and\n\\emph{obligation structure} name possible formal shapes.  They become dangerous\nwhen their mathematical status is unclear or when their names make unproved\ndata look like acceptable hypotheses of a source theorem.\n\n\\paragraph{Bridge.}\nA bridge should be a transport theorem between two already defined\nmathematical forms: for example, a tensor-placement identity, a conversion\nbetween two equivalent consistency relations, or a statement translating a\nsource object into a formal representation.  A bridge is harmless only after it\nis proved from previously available assumptions.  It becomes proof debt when it\nis assumed because the transport has not yet been proved.  It becomes theorem\ndrift when the assumed bridge is added to a paper-facing theorem.\n\n\\paragraph{Residual.}\nA residual is a named remainder after part of an argument has been performed.\nIt is often a useful way to record the exact missing target after a completed\nconstruction.  A residual may appear as the conclusion of a helper theorem or\nas the input of a quarantined conditional helper.  It is not a permissible new\nassumption on a paper theorem unless the paper itself assumes that residual.\n\n\\paragraph{Input.}\nAn input is a named bundle of data or hypotheses consumed by a construction or\nconditional helper.  It is harmless only when each load-bearing field is either\npart of the source hypotheses or is produced by an earlier theorem.  It becomes\nproof debt when the bundle is merely assumed because the construction of its\nfields is missing.  It becomes theorem drift when such a bundle is added to the\npublic statement of a source theorem.\n\n\\paragraph{Repair.}\nA repair is a mathematical construction which replaces an approximate or\npartial object by a better object, usually with a quantitative estimate.  In\nthe low individual degree test formalization, projectivization and\northonormalization repairs are genuine mathematical operations.  A repair\nshould therefore appear as a construction or as a theorem discharging the\ncorresponding obligation.  If a theorem assumes the output of the repair instead\nof constructing it, that theorem is conditional on the repair.\n\n\\paragraph{Obligation structure.}\nAn obligation structure is a record whose fields are the data and estimates\nneeded by a later construction.  This is acceptable only as an internal target\nor as a hypothesis of a conditional helper.  Such a structure becomes statement\ndrift if it is added to a paper-facing theorem instead of being constructed\ninside the proof.  The review question is whether every load-bearing field is\nproved from the source hypotheses or is explicitly tracked as a missing\nobligation.\n\n\\section{The main failure mode}\n\nSuppose the paper proves\n\\[\n  H \\Longrightarrow C.\n\\]\nDuring formalization, the proof may need an intermediate assertion \\(B\\).  The\npaper theorem should be represented as\n\\[\n  H \\Longrightarrow B \\Longrightarrow C\n  \\quad\\text{inside the proof,}\n\\]\nwhere \\(B\\) is obtained by a lemma or theorem from \\(H\\).  The following\npublic statement is a different theorem:\n\\[\n  H \\land B \\Longrightarrow C.\n\\]\nIt is not unsound in \\Lean{}, but it is not the paper theorem.  It says that the\nconclusion follows if the missing bridge data is supplied.  Such a theorem is a\nconditional helper, even if its conclusion looks exactly like the paper's\nconclusion.\n\nThis is the situation colloquially described as ``adding a bridge\nhypothesis''.  More precisely, an unproved intermediate step has been promoted\nfrom the proof body to the theorem's assumptions.  The correction is not to hide\nthe hypothesis under a different structure name.  The correction is to keep a\npaper-facing theorem with the source statement and move the missing step to a\nnamed internal proof obligation.\n\n\\section{Faithful boundary hypotheses}\n\nNot every extra formal hypothesis is a theorem drift.  Some hypotheses are\nfaithful boundary conditions introduced by formal encoding.  Examples include\nnonnegativity needed for a real power, positivity needed to divide by a\nquantity, finiteness and nonemptiness of an index type, a field-model instance,\nor decidability instances required by \\Lean{}.  Such hypotheses are acceptable\nwhen they express part of the mathematical ambient setting or make explicit a\ncondition used implicitly in the paper.\n\nThe distinction is load-bearing.  A faithful boundary hypothesis describes the\ndomain in which the paper's objects live.  A proof-debt hypothesis supplies a\nmathematical step that the proof should derive.  If removing the hypothesis\nleaves an unproved construction or estimate from the paper proof, then the\nhypothesis is proof debt, not a boundary condition.\n\n\\section{Definition drift and subtree repair}\n\nDefinition drift is especially dangerous because it propagates.  If a\ndefinition is changed so that it no longer denotes the object in the paper,\nthen every downstream theorem using that definition may continue to compile\nwhile proving statements about the wrong object.  Downstream theorem statements\ncan then be repaired piecemeal, but the development remains unstable because\nthe wrong definition is still upstream.\n\nWhen a definition mismatch is found, the repair should proceed by a subtree\nprotocol.\n\n\\begin{enumerate}\n  \\item Identify the source object and the formal object precisely.\n  \\item Freeze a source-faithful definition or state an adapter theorem\n  relating the existing definition to the source object.\n  \\item Recheck the downstream theorem chain against that definition or adapter.\n  \\item Re-formalize the affected subtree from the corrected interface, rather\n  than adding local hypotheses to each downstream theorem.\n  \\item If a downstream proof cannot be completed, record the missing obligation\n  at the lowest point where the paper proof needs it.\n\\end{enumerate}\n\nThis is slower than editing a final theorem signature, but it prevents a local\ndefinition error from becoming a global theorem-statement error.\n\n\\section{Allowed shapes}\n\n\\begin{center}\n\\begin{tabular}{p{0.24\\linewidth}p{0.31\\linewidth}p{0.32\\linewidth}}\n\\textbf{Shape} & \\textbf{Allowed use} & \\textbf{Forbidden use} \\\\\n\\hline\nPaper-facing theorem & Matches the source statement up to faithful encoding &\nCarries non-paper bridge, residual, repair, input, obligation-structure, or\nproof-obligation hypotheses \\\\\nSource-shaped theorem with a tracked \\verb|sorry| & Default repair when the\nsource proof is blocked but the statement is known & Replaced by a strengthened\ntheorem statement merely to keep the file compiling \\\\\nConditional helper & Temporary quarantine for substantial proof content whose\nremaining named obligation has not yet been discharged & Introduced merely to\navoid a \\verb|sorry|, or linked as the source theorem or marked as\nproof-complete for that theorem \\\\\nObligation discharger theorem & Constructs the obligation from paper hypotheses &\nMerely restates the obligation as an assumption \\\\\nInput bundle & Collects produced data for a local construction & Is assumed by a\nsource theorem instead of being produced \\\\\nObligation structure & Bundles constructed data and estimates & Hides unproved\nfields that are then assumed by a source theorem \\\\\nPaper-gap note & Documents a real mathematical or formal-statement divergence &\nJustifies silent statement drift without a repair plan\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{center}\n\n\\section{Protocol for a blocked proof}\n\nWhen a source-labelled proof is blocked, use the following order.\n\n\\begin{enumerate}\n  \\item Read the cited source statement and the proof passage in\n  \\path{references/ldt-paper/}.\n  \\item Write the paper theorem form, the current \\Lean{} theorem form, and the\n  first missing intermediate assertion.\n  \\item Decide whether the missing assertion is a faithful boundary condition,\n  a representation adapter, an ordinary lemma from the paper proof, or a real\n  paper-gap discrepancy.\n  \\item If it is an ordinary lemma or adapter, create a named theorem which\n  discharges that obligation.  Do not add it to the source theorem as a new\n  hypothesis.\n  \\item Keep the source-labelled theorem itself in the source form, even if its\n  proof must contain a tracked \\verb|sorry|.  This is the default repair when\n  the missing assertion has not yet been proved.\n  \\item Create a conditional helper only to quarantine substantial proof content\n  that already exists and would otherwise be lost.  Do not create such a helper\n  merely to avoid a \\verb|sorry| or to keep making progress.  If a conditional\n  helper remains, give it a conditional name, keep it separate from the\n  paper-facing theorem, and record the obligation discharger that must eliminate\n  it.\n  \\item If the source and formal statements genuinely differ, write or update a\n  note under \\path{docs/paper-gaps/} before marking the statement as aligned.\n  \\item Update the blueprint so that paper labels point only to paper-facing\n  declarations.  Conditional helpers belong in remarks or implementation\n  notes, not in the source theorem block.\n\\end{enumerate}\n\n\\section{Retirement criterion}\n\nAn auxiliary declaration should be removed from the main blueprint route, or\nrenamed and documented as a purely internal lemma, when all three of the\nfollowing conditions hold:\n\\begin{enumerate}\n  \\item it is not a statement in the cited paper and is not an explicitly cited\n        outside result;\n  \\item no current proof of a paper-level target needs it as stated;\n  \\item it assumes stronger proof data, finite-length data, completion data,\n        repair data, synchronization data, or package fields than the paper\n        proof requires.\n\\end{enumerate}\nIf such a declaration is still useful as a formal intermediate result, it\nshould remain a lemma or a visibly conditional helper with a planned discharge.\nIt should not be a headline replacement for the paper theorem, and it should\nnot support a source-labelled blueprint \\verb|\\leanok| claim.\n\n\\section{Review questions}\n\nA reviewer should first compare every paper-labelled declaration with the cited\nsource statement, checking both hypotheses and conclusion up to faithful formal\nencoding.  Bridge, residual, repair, input, obligation-structure, and\nproof-obligation assumptions should be absent from paper-facing theorem\nsignatures unless they occur in the paper.  If a conditional helper remains,\nits name should be explicitly conditional and it should not support a source\ntheorem \\verb|\\leanok| claim.\nEach load-bearing obligation-structure or input field should have a theorem\ndischarging it, a tracked issue, or an explicit \\verb|sorry| at the obligation\nsite.  When a definition has changed, the downstream subtree should be checked\nagainst the corrected definition rather than patched locally.  Finally, if the\nformal statement genuinely differs from the source statement, a paper-gap note\nshould explain the mathematical difference and give a plan to remove or justify\nit.\n\n\\section{Conclusion}\n\nThe project should prefer visible proof obligations over invisible statement\ndrift.  A tracked \\verb|sorry| in the source-shaped theorem, or in the lowest\nnamed internal obligation needed by its proof, is less misleading than a source\ntheorem whose assumptions have been strengthened.  Conditional helpers are not a\nnormal substitute for unfinished proofs; they are temporary quarantines for\nsubstantial proof content, and they must remain conditional until the missing\nobligation is discharged.  The paper-facing declaration is reserved for the\ntheorem proved by the paper, or for a documented corrected version whose\nmathematical difference is explicit.\n\n\\end{document}\n# Mathematical Language Guidelines\n\nMIPStarRE Lean names and documentation should be written for readers comparing\nthe formalization with the paper and blueprint.\n\nThis is a project-local supplement to the Mathlib-derived documentation,\nnaming, and style guides in the lean-conventions skill's `MATHLIB_doc`,\n`MATHLIB_naming`, and `MATHLIB_style` references.\n\n## Scope\n\nThese guidelines apply to:\n\n- public Lean declaration names and namespace names;\n- module docstrings;\n- declaration docstrings;\n- documentation-visible section comments;\n- explanatory comments that describe the mathematical role of a declaration.\n- blueprint prose and formalization-support notes;\n- issue titles and issue bodies;\n- PR titles and PR descriptions.\n\n## Source of Truth\n\nUse terminology from the following sources, in this order:\n\n1. `references/ldt-paper/`\n2. `blueprint/src/chapter/`\n3. established local conventions in nearby Lean files\n\nWhen the paper has a term for the object, use that term. For Section 5, for\nexample, prefer orthogonalization lemma, truncation function, rounding to\nprojectors, rank reduction, and completing to measurement.\n\n## Reference Notation And Terminology\n\nThe notation and terminology of the original reference are the default for\nreader-facing mathematical text.  A reader should be able to compare a Lean\ndocstring, blueprint paragraph, issue, or PR description with the cited source\nwithout first learning a private vocabulary used by the formalization.\n\nWhen Lean must use a different name or representation, define the deviation in a\nlocation which future readers can find from the affected statement.  Use the\nfirst applicable location in the following order:\n\n1. the declaration docstring of the public object whose name or representation\n   differs from the paper;\n2. the module docstring of the defining Lean file, when the deviation concerns a\n   family of declarations in that file;\n3. the relevant blueprint paragraph, when the notation appears only in the\n   blueprint;\n4. a report under `docs/reports/` or `docs/paper-gaps/`, when the deviation is a\n   larger discrepancy between the paper, blueprint, and Lean.\n\nThe explanation should say:\n\n- the notation or term used in the paper;\n- the Lean object or name which represents it;\n- the mathematical reason for the difference, if there is one;\n- the scope in which the replacement should be used.\n\nA PR description may mention the deviation, but it should not be the only place\nwhere future readers can learn it.\n\nFormalization-only auxiliary lemmas should be introduced as such.  Their prose\nshould name the nearby paper equation, theorem, or construction they support,\nrather than presenting the auxiliary name as paper terminology.\n\n## Naming Norm\n\nNames and prose should describe the mathematical object, hypothesis, or\nconclusion. They should not encode the history of how the formalization was\nassembled.\n\nAvoid presenting words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`, `raw`,\n`oneShot`, or `liveBlock` as mathematical terminology unless the cited source\nuses them with that meaning. Likewise, avoid implementation-local substitutes\nsuch as `projectivization` or `spectral truncation` when the paper gives a\nclearer phrase.\n\nThis is a general rule for the repository, not only a rule for file splits.\nModule names, namespace names, public declarations, theorem fields, docstrings,\nblueprint-facing names, issue titles, and spec documents should name the\nmathematical layer under discussion, not the local workflow step, paper line\nnumber, or implementation history.\n\n### Concrete examples\n\nThe table below illustrates the naming norm with examples patterned on the\ncodebase and on names seen during review. consolidated into a single\nshared helper in an appropriate common module. If the\n   types differ only by a chapter-specific parameterization (e.g.,\n   `SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι` vs `SubMeas (Point params) ι`),\n   parameterize the shared helper over that type via a `variable` or\n   explicit argument.\n2. **Find the right home.**  Prefer a module that is already imported by\n   both call sites. This is different from a documented public wrapper allowed in the\nshared-helper procedure above: a wrapper must preserve a paper-facing or\nblueprint-facing term and must say why the alias exists.\n\n## Review Checklist\n\nReviewers should use this checklist when examining public names and\ndocumentation prose. Are process words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`,\n      `raw`, `oneShot`, or `liveBlock` used as mathematical terms when the\n      source does not use them that way?\n- [ ] **Deviation documented.**  If a Lean name or representation differs from\n      the paper, is the deviation documented in a declaration docstring,\n      module docstring, blueprint paragraph, or `docs/paper-gaps/` note, in\n      that order of preference?\n- [ ] **Auxiliary lemmas.**  Are formalization-only auxiliary lemmas introduced\n      as such, with prose naming the nearby paper equation, theorem, or\n      construction they support?\n- [ ] **Shared helpers.**  Does the PR introduce a helper that already exists\n      (or near-exists) in another chapter-local leaf?  If so, has it been\n      consolidated into a common module with a mathematical name?\n- [ ] **Legacy IDs.**  If a legacy Lean identifier is mentioned, is the\n      mathematical object described in paper terminology? Statement-level `\\leanok`\n158-  is acceptable only when the Lean statement is intentionally recorded but the\n159-  proof remains tracked as incomplete.\n160-\n161-## Blueprint Structure\n162-- `content.tex` is a router: `\\input{chapter/ch01_intro}` etc.\n163-- Each chapter is a separate file in `chapter/`\n164-- Definitions/theorems numbered within chapters: `\\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}[chapter]`\n165-\n166-## Lean Blueprint Macros\n167-- `\\lean{Namespace.DeclName}` — links to Lean declaration\n168-- `\\leanok` — context-sensitive marker; see \"Statement-level vs proof-level `\\leanok`\" below\n169-- `\\uses{label1, label2}` — declares dependency edges for the graph\n170-- `\\notready` — marks as not ready for formalization (orange in graph)\n171-- `\\mathlibok` — already in Mathlib (dark green in graph; see legend note below)\n172-\n173-### Statement-level vs proof-level `\\leanok`\n174-\n175-`\\leanok` is context-sensitive for human review and graph interpretation. The \\emph{generalized Pauli\n   559\t\tobservables over $\\F_p$} are the unitaries on $\\C^{\\F_p}$ given by\n   560\t\t\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:pauli-fp}\n   561\t\t\t\\sigma^X(a) = \\sum_{j \\in \\F_p} \\ket{j + a}\\bra{j}\n   562\t\t\t\\qquad \\text{and} \\qquad\n   563\t\t\t\\sigma^Z(b) = \\sum_{j \\in \\F_p} \\omega^{bj} \\ket{j}\\bra{j}\n   564\t\t\\end{equation}\n   565\t\tfor $a, b \\in \\F_p$, with arithmetic over $\\F_p$. Their common eigenbases consist of the vectors\n   578\t\t$\\ket{e_W}$, labeled by $e \\in \\F_q$ and $W \\in \\{X, Z\\}$, given by\n   579\t\t\\[\n   580\t\t\t\\ket{e_X} = \\frac{1}{\\sqrt{q}} \\sum_{j \\in \\F_q}\n   581\t\t\t\\omega^{-\\tr(ej)} \\ket{j}\\;, \\qquad\n   582\t\t\t\\ket{e_Z} = \\ket{e}\\;;\n   583\t\t\\]\n   584\t\tthe Fourier transform\n   585\t\t\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:fourier-f}\n   586\t\t\tF = \\frac{1}{\\sqrt{q}} \\sum_{a, b \\in \\F_q}\n   587\t\t\t\\omega^{-\\tr(ab)} \\ket{a}\\bra{b}\n   588\t\t\\end{equation}\n   589\t\tmaps the computational ($Z$) eigenbasis to the $X$ eigenbasis. By the explicit\n   621\t\t\t      definitions each $\\tau^W(a)$ is unitary, and its eigenvalues are\n   622\t\t\t      $p$-th roots of unity.\n   623\t\t\t\\item For all $a, b \\in \\F_q^n$,\n   624\t\t\t      % Paper equation label kept on the display it names.\n   625\t\t\t      \\begin{equation}\\label{eq:twisted-fq}\n   626\t\t\t\t      \\tau^X(a)\\, \\tau^Z(b)\n   627\t\t\t\t      = \\omega^{-\\tr(a \\cdot b)}\\, \\tau^Z(b)\\, \\tau^X(a)\\;,\n   628\t\t\t      \\end{equation}\n   629\t\t\t      where $a \\cdot b = \\sum_{i=1}^n a_i b_i \\in \\F_q$. The case\n   630\t\t\t      $q = p$, $n = 1$ reads\n   631\t\t\t      \\begin{equation}\\label{eq:twisted-fp}\n   632\t\t\t\t      \\sigma^X(a)\\, \\sigma^Z(b)\n   633\t\t\t\t      = \\omega^{-ab}\\, \\sigma^Z(b)\\, \\sigma^X(a)\n   634\t\t\t\t      \\qquad \\text{for all } a, b \\in \\F_p\\;.\n   635\t\t\t      \\end{equation}\n   636\t\t\\end{enumerate}\n   637\t\\end{lemma}\n   638\t\\begin{proof}\n   639\t\t\\uses{def:generalized-pauli, def:subfield-trace}\n   640\t\tAll identities are verified on computational basis states. For the product\n   641\t\trelations with $W = X$, shifting twice by $a'$ and $a$ equals shifting by\n   642\t\t$a + a'$; with $W = Z$, the phases $\\omega^{\\tr(aj)}\\omega^{\\tr(a'j)}$\n   643\t\tcombine by $\\F_q$-linearity of the trace, and the power relation follows by\n   644\t\titerating. The multi-qudit relation\n   648\t\tfollows by applying the scalar relation factor by factor and summing the\n   649\t\texponents, using $\\tr(a \\cdot b) = \\sum_i \\tr(a_i b_i)$. For $q = p$ the\n   650\t\ttrace is the identity map, which gives \\eqref{eq:twisted-fp}.\n   651\t\\end{proof}\n   652\t\n   653\t\\begin{lemma}[Fourier cancellation over a subspace]\\label{lem:cancellation}\n   654\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ffChar_dotProduct_submodule_expect_eq_zero}\n   655\t\t\\leanok\n   656\t\t\\uses{def:dot-product-orthogonal, def:subfield-trace}\n   657\t\tLet $V$ be a subspace of $\\F_q^k$ and let $\\omega = e^{2\\pi i/p}$, where\n   658\t\t$p$ is the characteristic of $\\F_q$ and $\\tr = \\tr_{q \\to p}$. This is the content of the\n   712\tnext lemma, which is what allows the Pauli basis test to self-test Pauli\n   713\tobservables and maximally entangled states over \\emph{qubits}\n   714\t(Chapter~\\ref{chap:qpbt-test}).\n   715\t\n   716\t\\begin{lemma}[Qudit-to-qubit isomorphism]\\label{lem:pauli-binary}\n   717\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.qubitPauliProj, MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_qubitIsometry}\n   718\t\t\\leanok\n   719\t\t\\uses{def:admissible-size, def:subfields-kappa, def:binary-representation,\n   720\t\t\tdef:generalized-pauli, def:EPR}\n   721\t\tFor all admissible field sizes $q = 2^k$ and integers $L \\ge 0$, there\n   722\t\texists an isomorphism $\\phi : (\\C^q)^{\\ot L} \\to (\\C^2)^{\\ot Lk}$ such that\n   723\t\t\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:epr-q-to-epr-2}\n   724\t\t\t\\phi \\ot \\phi\\, \\ket{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\\ot L}\n   725\t\t\t= \\ket{\\mathrm{EPR}_2}^{\\ot Lk}\n   726\t\t\\end{equation}\n   727\t\t(applying the natural identifications between\n   728\t\t$(\\C^q)^{\\ot L} \\ot (\\C^q)^{\\ot L}$ and $(\\C^q \\ot \\C^q)^{\\ot L}$, and\n   729\t\tbetween $(\\C^2)^{\\ot Lk} \\ot (\\C^2)^{\\ot Lk}$ and\n   730\t\t$(\\C^2 \\ot \\C^2)^{\\ot Lk}$). This bound must be derived from point consistency and\n   273\t\tSchwartz--Zippel; it is not an additional extraction hypothesis.\n   274\t\\end{lemma}\n   275\t\n   276\t% Following the source, the next lemma is stated after\n   277\t% lem:qld-construct-the-paulis, whose proof invokes it; its own proof\n   278\t% depends only on lem:qld-4-7 and lem:qld-comm-cons, so there is no\n   279\t% circularity.\n   280\tLemmas~\\ref{lem:qld-4-7} and~\\ref{lem:qld-comm-cons} imply the following two estimates, which were used in the proof of Lemma~\\ref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis}.\n   281\t\n   282\t\\begin{lemma}[The marginals absorb the point measurements]\\label{lem:qld-constructing-the-paulis-helper}\n   283\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.sum_marginalPoly_pointMeas_approx_id}\n   284\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.marginalPoly_sub_pointMeas_approx_zero}\n   285\t\t\\leanok\n   286\t\t\\uses{def:s-w-marginals, def:expanded-point-measurement, def:expanded-state, def:povm-distance, lem:qld-4-7, def:symmetric-equivalents}\n   287\t\tFor $W \\in \\{X,Z\\}$, on average over uniformly random $u \\in \\F_q^m$,\n   288\t\t\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:qld-sg-cons}\n   289\t\t\t\\sum_g (\\hat{S}^W_g)_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'} \\ot (\\hat{M}^{(\\mathrm{Point},W),u}_{g(u)})_{\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{A}''} \\approx_{\\delta_P^{\\mathrm{id}}} \\Id\n   290\t\t\\end{equation}\n   291\t\tand\n   292\t\t\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:qld-sg-cons2}\n   293\t\t\t\\bigl(\\hat{S}^W_g \\cdot (\\Id - \\hat{M}^{(\\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_{g(u)})\\bigr)_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'} \\approx_{\\delta_P^{\\mathrm{ann}}} 0\\;,\n   294\t\t\\end{equation}\n   295\t\twhere the answer summation is over $g \\in \\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\\F_q)$. Furthermore, all symmetric equivalents of these approximations also hold (Definition~\\ref{def:symmetric-equivalents}).\n   296\t\\end{lemma}\n   297\t\\begin{proof}\n   298\t\t\\uses{lem:qld-4-7, fact:agreement, fact:add-a-proj, def:bracket, lem:qld-comm-cons}\n   299\t\tThe point-consistency conclusion of Lemma~\\ref{lem:qld-4-7} states that, on average over $u \\in \\F_q^m$,\n   300\t\t\\[\n   301\t\t\t\\bra{\\hat\\psi} \\sum_g (\\hat{S}^W_g)_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'} \\ot (\\hat{M}^{(\\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_{g(u)})_{\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{A}''} \\ket{\\hat\\psi} \\geq 1 - \\delta_G\\;,\n   302\t\t\\]\n   303\t\twhich says exactly that the operator on the left-hand side of \\eqref{eq:qld-sg-cons} is $\\delta_G$-consistent with $\\Id$; Lemma~\\ref{fact:agreement} and the universal-factor enlargement give the $\\approx_{\\delta_P}$ statement \\eqref{eq:qld-sg-cons}. For \\eqref{eq:qld-sg-cons2}, the same consistency, written with the coarse-graining $\\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]} = \\sum_{g : g(u) = a} \\hat{S}^W_g$ as $(\\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]})_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'} \\approx_{O(\\delta_G)} (\\hat{M}^{(\\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_{a})_{\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{A}''}$ with answer summation over $a \\in \\F_q$, is left-multiplied by $(\\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]})_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'}$ using Lemma~\\ref{fact:add-a-proj}; moving $\\hat{M}^{(\\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_a$ from registers $\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{A}''$ to $\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'$ costs a further $\\eps$ by Cauchy--Schwarz together with the self-consistency of the $\\hat{M}^{(\\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_a$ (Lemma~\\ref{lem:qld-comm-cons}), giving\n   304\t\t\\[\n   305\t\t\t(\\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]})_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'} \\approx_{O(\\delta_G + \\eps)} (\\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]} \\cdot \\hat{M}^{(\\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_{a})_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'}\\;.\n   306\t\t\\]\n   307\t\tExpanding\n   308\t\t\\[\n   309\t\t\t\\E_u \\sum_g \\bigl\\| (\\hat{S}^W_{g} \\cdot (\\Id - \\hat{M}^{(\\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_{g(u)}))_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'} \\ket{\\hat\\psi} \\bigr\\|^2\n   310\t\t\t= \\E_u \\sum_a \\bra{\\hat\\psi} \\bigl((\\Id - \\hat{M}^{(\\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_{a}) \\cdot \\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]} \\cdot (\\Id - \\hat{M}^{(\\mathrm{Point}, W), u}_{a})\\bigr)_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'} \\ket{\\hat\\psi}\n   311\t\t\\]\n   312\t\tand bounding the right-hand side by $O(\\delta_G + \\eps)$ using the two approximations above yields \\eqref{eq:qld-sg-cons2} at scale $\\delta_P$. The symmetric equivalents follow by the same argument with the register bipartitions interchanged.\n   313\t\\end{proof}\n   314\t\n   315\t\\section{The swap unitaries and the extraction of the Pauli group}\n   316\t\n   317\t\\begin{definition}[The swap unitaries]\\label{def:v-swap-unitary}\n   318\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.swapUnitary}\n   319\t\t\\leanok\n   320\t\t\\uses{lem:qld-4-7, def:generalized-pauli, def:qld-full-field-decoder}\n   321\t\tDefine the linear map\n   322\t\t\\[\n   323\t\t\tV_{\\mathrm{A}} = \\sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'} \\ot \\bigl(\\tau^X(\\mathrm{Dec}(g_Z)) \\, \\tau^Z(\\mathrm{Dec}(g_X))\\bigr)_{\\mathrm{A}''}\\;,\n   324\t\t\\]\n   325\t\twhere $\\tau^X(\\cdot)$ and $\\tau^Z(\\cdot)$ are the generalized Pauli observables acting on $(\\C^q)^{\\ot M}$; note that the argument of $\\tau^X$ is $\\mathrm{Dec}(g_Z)$ and the argument of $\\tau^Z$ is $\\mathrm{Dec}(g_X)$. The map $V_{\\mathrm{B}}$, acting on registers $\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{B}'\\mathrm{B}''$, is defined analogously.\n   326\t\\end{definition}\n   327\t\n   328\t% In the source the following properties are established inline with the\n   329\t% definition of the swap unitaries; they are recorded here as a lemma.\n   330\t\\begin{lemma}[Unitarity and conjugation action of the swap unitaries]\\label{lem:v-swap-conjugation}\n   331\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.swapUnitary_mul_conjTranspose}\n   332\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.conjTranspose_mul_swapUnitary}\n   333\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.swapUnitary_conj_tildeObs}\n   334\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.swapUnitary_conj_tildeM}\n   335\t\t\\leanok\n   336\t\t\\uses{def:v-swap-unitary, def:tilde-w-observables, def:tilde-m-measurement, def:generalized-pauli, def:indicator-vector, def:bracket}\n   337\t\tThe maps $V_{\\mathrm{A}}$ and $V_{\\mathrm{B}}$ of Definition~\\ref{def:v-swap-unitary} are unitaries acting on registers $\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'\\mathrm{A}''$ and $\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{B}'\\mathrm{B}''$ respectively, and their conjugation action is exact, as follows. For all $W \\in \\{X,Z\\}$, $j \\in \\{0,\\ldots,t-1\\}$, and $\\tilde{u} \\in \\F_q^M$,\n   338\t\t\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:v-swap-obs-conjugation}\n   339\t\t\tV_{\\mathrm{A}} \\, \\tilde{W}^j(\\tilde{u}) \\, V_{\\mathrm{A}}^\\dagger = \\Id_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'} \\ot \\bigl( \\tau^W(e_j \\tilde{u}) \\bigr)_{\\mathrm{A}''}\n   340\t\t\t\\qquad \\text{and} \\qquad\n   341\t\t\tV_{\\mathrm{B}} \\, \\tilde{W}^j(\\tilde{u}) \\, V_{\\mathrm{B}}^\\dagger = \\Id_{\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{B}'} \\ot \\bigl( \\tau^W(e_j \\tilde{u}) \\bigr)_{\\mathrm{B}''}\\;,\n   342\t\t\\end{equation}\n   343\t\tand for all $W \\in \\{X,Z\\}$, $u \\in \\F_q^m$, and $a \\in \\F_q$,\n   344\t\t\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:qld-unitary-6}\n   345\t\t\tV_{\\mathrm{B}} \\, \\tilde{M}^{W,\\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a \\, V_{\\mathrm{B}}^\\dagger = \\Id_{\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{B}'} \\ot (\\tau^W_{[g_h(u)=a]})_{\\mathrm{B}''}\\;,\n   346\t\t\t\\qquad\n   347\t\t\t\\tau^W_{[g_h(u)=a]} = \\sum_{h \\,:\\, g_h(u) = a} \\tau^W_h\\;,\n   348\t\t\\end{equation}\n   349\t\ttogether with the analogous identity for $V_{\\mathrm{A}}$ on registers $\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'\\mathrm{A}''$.\n   350\t\\end{lemma}\n   351\t\\begin{proof}\n   352\t\t\\uses{lem:qld-4-7, lem:tildew-product-form, lem:twisted-commutation, def:v-swap-unitary, def:tilde-m-measurement, def:tau-dot-product-projector, def:indicator-vector, def:decoding-map, def:generalized-pauli}\n   353\t\tSince the measurement $\\{\\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}\\}$ is projective (Lemma~\\ref{lem:qld-4-7}) and the $\\tau^X, \\tau^Z$ observables are self-inverse,\n   354\t\t\\[\n   355\t\t\tV_{\\mathrm{A}} V_{\\mathrm{A}}^\\dagger = \\sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'} \\ot \\Id_{\\mathrm{A}''} = \\Id_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'\\mathrm{A}''}\\;,\n   356\t\t\\]\n   357\t\tand the same computation gives $V_{\\mathrm{A}}^\\dagger V_{\\mathrm{A}} = \\Id$, so $V_{\\mathrm{A}}$ is unitary; likewise $V_{\\mathrm{B}}$. For \\eqref{eq:v-swap-obs-conjugation}, conjugate the product form \\eqref{eq:tildewj-product-form} of $\\tilde{W}^j(\\tilde{u})$ (Lemma~\\ref{lem:tildew-product-form}): by the orthogonality of the projectors $\\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}$, only the diagonal terms survive, and the twisted commutation relation (Lemma~\\ref{lem:twisted-commutation})\n   358\t\t\\[\n   359\t\t\t\\tau^X(\\mathrm{Dec}(g_Z)) \\, \\tau^Z(\\mathrm{Dec}(g_X)) \\, \\tau^W(e_j \\tilde{u}) = (-1)^{\\tr( e_j(\\mathrm{Dec}(g_W) \\cdot \\tilde{u}))} \\, \\tau^W(e_j \\tilde{u}) \\, \\tau^X(\\mathrm{Dec}(g_Z)) \\, \\tau^Z(\\mathrm{Dec}(g_X))\n   360\t\t\\]\n   361\t\tcancels the sign $(-1)^{\\tr(e_j (\\mathrm{Dec}(g_W) \\cdot \\tilde{u}))}$ term by term, leaving $\\sum_{g_X,g_Z} \\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z} \\ot \\tau^W(e_j \\tilde{u}) = \\Id \\ot \\tau^W(e_j \\tilde{u})$. For \\eqref{eq:qld-unitary-6}, expand $\\tilde{M}^{W,\\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a$ by \\eqref{eq:tilde_M} and \\eqref{eq:def-tauwu}; by the orthogonality of the $\\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}$, conjugation replaces, in the term of $\\hat{S}^W_g$, each projector $\\tau^W_h$ by $\\tau^W_{h + \\mathrm{Dec}(g)}$, using the identities $\\tau^X(s)\\, \\tau^Z_h \\,\\tau^X(s)^\\dagger = \\tau^Z_{h+s}$ and $\\tau^Z(s)\\, \\tau^X_h\\, \\tau^Z(s)^\\dagger = \\tau^X_{h+s}$. Substituting $h' = h + \\mathrm{Dec}(g)$ turns the constraint $h \\cdot \\mathrm{ind}_m(u) = (\\mathrm{Dec}(g) \\cdot \\mathrm{ind}_m(u)) - a$ into $h' \\cdot \\mathrm{ind}_m(u) = -a = a$, since $\\F_q$ has characteristic $2$; the quantity $\\mathrm{Dec}(g) \\cdot \\mathrm{ind}_m(u)$ cancels exactly, so no relation between it and $g(u)$ is used (Remark~\\ref{rem:qld-decoding-identity}). Since $h' \\cdot \\mathrm{ind}_m(u) = g_{h'}(u)$ \\eqref{eq:low-degree-encoding-definition}, summing over $g$ gives \\eqref{eq:qld-unitary-6}; the computation for $V_{\\mathrm{A}}$ on registers $\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'\\mathrm{A}''$ is identical.\n   362\t\\end{proof}\n   363\t\n   364\t\\begin{lemma}[Extraction of the EPR state and the Pauli observables]\\label{lem:qld-unitary}\n   365\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ExtractionWitness}\n   366\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.deltaExtract}\n   367\t\t\\uses{lem:qld-4-7, def:v-swap-unitary, def:expanded-state, lem:projective-strategy-setup, def:generalized-pauli, def:EPR, def:povm-distance}\n   368\t\tThere is a universal constant $C_{\\mathrm{ext}}\\geq1$. Set\n   369\t\t\\[\n   370\t\t\t\\delta_P^{\\mathrm{ext}}=C_{\\mathrm{ext}}B,\n   371\t\t\t\\qquad\n   372\t\t\t\\delta_{\\mathrm{qld}}=C_{\\mathrm{ext}}\n   373\t\t\t\\left((\\delta_P^{\\mathrm{ext}})^{1/4}+\\frac{md}{q}\\right).\n   374\t\t\\]\n   375\t\tThere exist unitaries $V_{\\mathrm{A}}$ acting on registers $\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'\\mathrm{A}''$ and $V_{\\mathrm{B}}$ acting on registers $\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{B}'\\mathrm{B}''$, such that the following hold.\n   376\t\t\\begin{enumerate}\n   377\t\t\t\\item There exists a state $\\ket{\\mathrm{aux}}$ on registers $\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{B}'$ such that\n   378\t\t\t\\[\n   379\t\t\t\t\\bigl\\| V_{\\mathrm{A}} \\ot V_{\\mathrm{B}} \\ket{\\hat{\\psi}}_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'\\mathrm{A}''\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{B}'\\mathrm{B}''} - \\ket{\\mathrm{aux}}_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{B}'} \\ot \\ket{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\\ot M}_{\\mathrm{A}''\\mathrm{B}''} \\bigr\\|^2 \\leq \\delta_{\\mathrm{qld}}\\;.\n   380\t\t\t\\]\n   381\t\t\t\\item For $W \\in \\{X,Z\\}$,\n   382\t\t\t\\begin{align*}\n   383\t\t\t\tV_{\\mathrm{A}} \\, \\bigl(M^{(\\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h \\bigr)_{\\mathrm{A}} \\, V_{\\mathrm{A}}^\\dagger &\\approx_{\\delta_{\\mathrm{qld}}} \\Id_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'} \\ot (\\tau^W_h)_{\\mathrm{A}''}\\;, \\\\\n   384\t\t\t\tV_{\\mathrm{B}} \\, \\bigl(M^{(\\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h \\bigr)_{\\mathrm{B}} \\, V_{\\mathrm{B}}^\\dagger &\\approx_{\\delta_{\\mathrm{qld}}} \\Id_{\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{B}'} \\ot (\\tau^W_h)_{\\mathrm{B}''}\\;,\n   385\t\t\t\\end{align*}\n   386\t\t\twhere the $\\approx$ statements hold with respect to the state $\\ket{\\mathrm{aux}}_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{B}'} \\ot \\ket{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\\ot M}_{\\mathrm{A}''\\mathrm{B}''}$, with the answer summation over $h \\in \\F_q^{M}$ and no average over questions.\n   387\t\t\\end{enumerate}\n   388\t\tThe unitaries may be taken to be $V_{\\mathrm{A}}$ and $V_{\\mathrm{B}}$ of Definition~\\ref{def:v-swap-unitary}.\n   389\t\tNo Lean declaration states this lemma. The only existence declaration available assumes the global polynomial-pair measurement of Lemma~\\ref{lem:qld-4-7} as data, instead of obtaining it from that lemma as the proof below does; it is therefore a conditional helper, it does not certify the statement above, and it is not linked here. The discrepancy and the source-facing declaration that must replace it are recorded in \\cite{gap:qpbt_extraction-transfer}.\n   390\t\\end{lemma}\n   391\t\\begin{proof}\n   392\t\t\\uses{def:v-swap-unitary, lem:v-swap-conjugation, lem:tildew-product-form, lem:qld-construct-the-paulis, lem:qld-win-implications, fact:triangle-for-simeq, def:bracket, lem:cancellation, lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree, lem:qld-4-7}\n   393\t\tFor the first item, the self-consistency of the observables $\\tilde{W}^j$ (Item~2 of Lemma~\\ref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis}) is equivalent, since these observables are Hermitian involutions (Lemma~\\ref{lem:tildew-product-form}), to $\\E_{j \\in \\{0,\\ldots,t-1\\}} \\E_{\\tilde{u} \\in \\F_q^M} \\bra{\\hat\\psi} \\tilde{W}^j(\\tilde{u}) \\ot \\tilde{W}^j(\\tilde{u}) \\ket{\\hat\\psi} \\geq 1 - \\delta_P/2$; setting $\\ket{\\vartheta} = V_{\\mathrm{A}} \\ot V_{\\mathrm{B}} \\ket{\\hat\\psi}$ and using the exact conjugation identities of Lemma~\\ref{lem:v-swap-conjugation}, this becomes $\\bra{\\vartheta} H_W \\ket{\\vartheta} \\geq 1 - \\delta_P/2$ for $W \\in \\{X,Z\\}$, where $H_W = \\E_j \\E_{\\tilde{u}} \\, \\tau^W(e_j \\tilde{u}) \\ot \\tau^W(e_j \\tilde{u}) = \\bigl( \\E_{s \\in \\F_q} \\tau^W(s) \\ot \\tau^W(s) \\bigr)^{\\ot M}$ by the tensor factorization of $\\tau^W(\\tilde{u})$ and the invariance of the uniform average over $s$ under $s \\mapsto e_j s$. By Lemma~\\ref{lem:cancellation}, $\\E_{s,s'} \\tau^X(s)\\tau^Z(s') \\ot \\tau^X(s)\\tau^Z(s') = \\ket{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}\\bra{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}$ on each pair of qudits, whence $H_X H_Z = \\ket{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}\\bra{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\\ot M}$. The bounds $\\| (\\Id - H_W)\\ket{\\vartheta} \\|^2 \\leq \\delta_P$ and $\\bra{\\vartheta} H_W^2 \\ket{\\vartheta} \\geq 1 - 2\\delta_P$, combined through the triangle inequality $\\| H_X \\ket{\\vartheta} - H_Z \\ket{\\vartheta} \\| \\leq 2\\sqrt{\\delta_P}$ (see Remark~\\ref{rem:qld-unitary-triangle-slip}), give $\\bra{\\vartheta} \\Id_{\\mathrm{A}\\mathrm{A}'\\mathrm{B}\\mathrm{B}'} \\ot (\\ket{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}\\bra{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\\ot M})_{\\mathrm{A}''\\mathrm{B}''} \\ket{\\vartheta} \\geq 1 - 4\\delta_P$.\n   394\t\t% Case distinction added: the source normalizes the projected vector\n   395\t\t% without ensuring that it is nonzero; see Remark rem:qld-unitary-triangle-slip.\n   396\t\tIf $\\delta_P > 1/8$, then, after enlarging the universal constant in $\\delta_{\\mathrm{qld}}$, both items of the lemma hold with $\\ket{\\mathrm{aux}}$ an arbitrary unit state, since their left-hand sides never exceed $4$; assume therefore $\\delta_P \\leq 1/8$. Then the vector $(\\bra{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\\ot M})_{\\mathrm{A}''\\mathrm{B}''} \\ket{\\vartheta}$ has squared norm at least $1 - 4\\delta_P \\geq 1/2 > 0$, and $\\ket{\\mathrm{aux}}$ may be defined as its normalization; the overlap of $\\ket{\\vartheta}$ with $\\ket{\\mathrm{aux}} \\ot \\ket{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\\ot M}$ equals the norm of that vector and is at least $\\sqrt{1 - 4\\delta_P} \\geq 1 - 4\\delta_P$, which yields the first item with a bound of $8\\delta_P = O(\\sqrt{\\delta_P})$. For the second item, Lemma~\\ref{lem:qld-win-implications} gives, on average over $u \\in \\F_q^m$, $M^{(\\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \\ot \\Id \\simeq_\\eps \\Id \\ot M^{(\\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a$ and $\\Id \\ot M^{(\\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a \\simeq_\\eps M^{(\\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a \\ot \\Id$, where $M^{(\\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} = \\sum_{h : g_h(u) = a} M^{(\\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h$; combining these with Item~1 of Lemma~\\ref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} by Lemma~\\ref{fact:triangle-for-simeq}, using $\\eps \\leq \\sqrt{\\eps} \\leq \\delta_P$, yields $M^{(\\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \\ot \\Id \\simeq_{\\sqrt{\\delta_P}} \\Id \\ot \\tilde{M}^{W,\\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a$. Writing $\\ket{\\Delta} = \\ket{\\mathrm{aux}} \\ot \\ket{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\\ot M}$, the quantity to be bounded for the $\\mathrm{A}$-side relation equals $2 - 2\\sum_h \\bra{\\Delta} V_{\\mathrm{A}} M^{(\\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h V_{\\mathrm{A}}^\\dagger \\ot (\\tau^W_h)_{\\mathrm{B}''} \\ket{\\Delta}$, since $(\\tau^W_h)_{\\mathrm{A}''} \\ket{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\\ot M} = (\\tau^W_h)_{\\mathrm{B}''} \\ket{\\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\\ot M}$. Replacing $(\\tau^W_h)_{\\mathrm{B}''}$ by the averaged coarse-graining $\\E_u \\sum_{h' : g_{h'}(u) = g_h(u)} (\\tau^W_{h'})_{\\mathrm{B}''}$ costs at most $md/q$ by Lemma~\\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree} (distinct $h \\neq h'$ have distinct encodings $g_h \\neq g_{h'}$, of total degree at most $md$), and by \\eqref{eq:qld-unitary-6} the resulting sum equals $\\E_u \\sum_{a} \\bra{\\Delta} V_{\\mathrm{A}} M^{(\\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} V_{\\mathrm{A}}^\\dagger \\ot V_{\\mathrm{B}} \\tilde{M}^{W,\\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a V_{\\mathrm{B}}^\\dagger \\ket{\\Delta}$. local maps are constructed from the global polynomial

/-- The concrete conclusion of `lem:qld-unitary`: the two swap maps extract an
EPR state and conjugate each player's total Pauli measurement to the canonical
Pauli projectors. The answer sum in `pauli_close` is over

Blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:348-375`; paper
`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685,1827-1859`. The swap maps
are `swapUnitary w .alice` and `swapUnitary w .bob`, defined from the
side-indexed global measurements, and use only the basis fixed by `P.model`.
-/
structure ExtractionWitness {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaS : ℝ}
    (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon) (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaS)
    (delta : ℝ) where
  /-- Each swap map is a right unitary. -/
  swap_right_unitary : ∀ side : PlayerSide,
    swapUnitary w side * (swapUnitary w side)ᴴ = 1
  /-- Each swap map is a left unitary. -/
  swap_left_unitary : ∀ side : PlayerSide,
    (swapUnitary w side)ᴴ * swapUnitary w side = 1
  /-- The auxiliary state on registers `AA'BB'`. -/
  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ
    (ExtractionAuxRegisters P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
  /-- The auxiliary state is normalized. -/
  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
  /-- Applying both concrete swap maps to the expanded state extracts the ideal
  auxiliary-state/EPR tensor product. -/
  state_close :
    ‖S.applyBoth (swapUnitary w .alice) (swapUnitary w .bob) S.psiHat -
        S.idealExpState aux‖ ^ 2 ≤ delta
  /-- On the ideal extracted state, conjugated total-Pauli effects are close to
  the canonical projectors, for both players and both Pauli bases. -/
  pauli_close : ∀ (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind),
    opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
      (fun (_ : Unit) (h : PauliRegister P) =>
        conjBy (S.placeSide side (swapUnitary w side))
          (S.placePlayer side ((S.pauliMeas side W).effect h)))
      (fun (_ : Unit) (h : PauliRegister P) =>
        S.placeExtractedRegister side (pauliProj W h))
      (S.idealExpState aux) ≤ delta

$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z,s}$ are combined into a sandwich POVM, the
resulting family is shown to satisfy an approximate linearity in the index
pair $(r,s)$, and the following result of Natarajan and
Vidick~\cite{Natarajan2017Linearity} converts approximate linearity into exact
linearity, from which a projective measurement with outcomes in $\F_q^2$ is
assembled by Fourier averaging.

\begin{theorem}[Quantum linearity test~\cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}]
	\label{thm:linearity}
	Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity} is stated in the form established by the
	argument of \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}, with the normalization of its
	distance bound corrected as described in
	Remark~\ref{rem:linearity-distance-normalization}. Three features are
	load-bearing for the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10}: the error is
	preserved without polynomial loss ($\delta$ in the hypothesis becomes
	$2\delta$ in the conclusion for the squared operator distance, and
	$\delta$ for the squared measurement distance, a constant factor absorbed
	by the relation $\approx_\delta$); the linearity of the
	$\{\mathcal{L}^u\}$ is exact and holds for all pairs $(u,u')$, not merely
	on average; and the hypothesis carries no upper bound on $\delta$, so the
	theorem may be applied separately for each pair $(x,z)$ with hypothesis
	error the conditional linearity defect given $(x,z)$, a quantity for
	which no a priori bound is available. The closeness of $\mathcal{L}^u$ to
	$\mathcal{O}^u$ is guaranteed on average over a uniformly random $u$
	only; this averaged form suffices because the $\mathcal{L}^u$ enter
	the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10} only through averages over $u$.
	The quotation of the theorem in \cite{Ji2020MIPStar} differs from the
	cited statement in three respects: it inserts the restriction
	$0 \le \delta \le 1$, which would block the fiberwise application
	just described; it places the closeness conclusion, together with the
	exact linearity, under the quantifier ``for all $u, u' \in \F_2^t$'',
	a strengthening of the theorem proved in
	\cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}; and it appends the identity
	$\mathcal{L}^u = \Id$ for $u = 0$. None of the three is
	reproduced here: the restriction is dropped, the pointwise closeness
	is not used, and the appended identity is instead derived from the
	conclusion, since exact linearity at $u = u' = 0$ gives
	$(\mathcal{L}^0)^2 = \mathcal{L}^0$, and an idempotent unitary equals
	the identity. The factor of two of
	Remark~\ref{rem:linearity-distance-normalization} is not one of these
	differences. It is a defect of the cited statement itself: the mean
	squared operator bound printed in
	\cite[Theorem~10]{Natarajan2017Linearity} is $\delta$, whereas the
	calculation behind \cite[equation~(3)]{Natarajan2017Linearity} bounds
	the mean squared distance between the associated binary projective
	measurements, which is half the squared operator distance; the

\title{Proof-Gap Protocol for Source-Faithful Formalization}
\author{}
\date{2026-05-11}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\section{Purpose}

This note fixes terminology for a recurring failure mode in the formalization
of the low individual degree test paper, \path{arXiv:2009.12982}.  It
complements the note-writing policy in \path{docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex} and
the source-statement audit tracked historically in \ghissue{1458}.  The current
source-boundary proof holes are tracked in \ghissue{1507} and \ghissue{422}.
A proof may be blocked at
an intermediate mathematical assertion.  If that assertion is added as a new
hypothesis to a theorem labelled as a paper theorem, the resulting \Lean{}
theorem
may be correct as a conditional statement, but it is no longer the theorem in
the cited source.  The apparent proof has not closed the paper theorem; it has
moved a proof obligation into the theorem statement.

The protocol below distinguishes such proof debt from legitimate formal
boundary conditions and from genuine mathematical corrections.  It is meant for
contributors and reviewers who must decide whether a bridge, residual, repair,
input, or obligation structure is a proved local construction, a tracked proof
gap, or statement drift which must be repaired before a theorem may be
advertised as a source theorem.  The default rule is restrictive: such data
must not be added to a paper-facing theorem unless it is part of the cited
source statement or a documented faithful encoding of its ambient hypotheses.

\section{Basic objects}

\paragraph{Source theorem.}
A source theorem is a theorem, lemma, proposition, or corollary in the paper
source under \path{references/ldt-paper/}.  Its hypotheses and conclusion are
the mathematical ground truth, subject only to faithful formal encoding and to
documented paper-gap corrections.

\paragraph{Paper-facing declaration.}
A \Lean{} declaration is paper-facing when it is named or cited as the
formalization of a source theorem, for instance through a blueprint
\verb|\lean{}| link on a theorem environment carrying a paper label.  Such a
declaration must match the source theorem in its public statement.  In
particular, it may not add an unproved bridge, residual, repair, input,
obligation structure, or other proof-obligation hypothesis which the paper does
not assume.

\paragraph{Proof obligation.}
A proof obligation is an intermediate assertion needed by the proof of a source
theorem.  It may be a construction, an estimate, a transport lemma, or a
comparison between two formal representations.  If the paper proves or invokes
this assertion, then the formalization should state it as a separate lemma or
theorem and prove it from the upstream hypotheses.

\paragraph{Obligation discharger.}
An obligation discharger is a theorem or definition which constructs a proof
obligation from the paper hypotheses already available at that point in the
argument.  This is the preferred representation of missing work.  If the proof
is not yet complete, the discharger may temporarily contain a tracked
\verb|sorry|, but the paper-facing theorem should call it rather than assume
its output as an additional theorem hypothesis.

\paragraph{Conditional helper.}
A conditional helper is a separately named theorem whose statement explicitly
assumes a proof obligation.  Names such as
\leanid{mainFormal\_ofInternalObligations},
\leanid{orthonormalization\_ofInput}, or names whose suffix advertises the
assumed obligation are permitted only when the declaration is not presented as
the source theorem.  A conditional helper is a quarantine for downstream proof
content; it does not close the source theorem.

\section{Bridge, residual, repair, input, and obligation structures}

The words \emph{bridge}, \emph{residual}, \emph{repair}, \emph{input}, and
\emph{obligation structure} name possible formal shapes.  They become dangerous
when their mathematical status is unclear or when their names make unproved
data look like acceptable hypotheses of a source theorem.

\paragraph{Bridge.}
A bridge should be a transport theorem between two already defined
mathematical forms: for example, a tensor-placement identity, a conversion
between two equivalent consistency relations, or a statement translating a
source object into a formal representation.  A bridge is harmless only after it
is proved from previously available assumptions.  It becomes proof debt when it
is assumed because the transport has not yet been proved.  It becomes theorem
drift when the assumed bridge is added to a paper-facing theorem.

\paragraph{Residual.}
A residual is a named remainder after part of an argument has been performed.
It is often a useful way to record the exact missing target after a completed
construction.  A residual may appear as the conclusion of a helper theorem or
as the input of a quarantined conditional helper.  It is not a permissible new
assumption on a paper theorem unless the paper itself assumes that residual.

\paragraph{Input.}
An input is a named bundle of data or hypotheses consumed by a construction or
conditional helper.  It is harmless only when each load-bearing field is either
part of the source hypotheses or is produced by an earlier theorem.  It becomes
proof debt when the bundle is merely assumed because the construction of its
fields is missing.  It becomes theorem drift when such a bundle is added to the
public statement of a source theorem.

\paragraph{Repair.}
A repair is a mathematical construction which replaces an approximate or
partial object by a better object, usually with a quantitative estimate.  In
the low individual degree test formalization, projectivization and
orthonormalization repairs are genuine mathematical operations.  A repair
should therefore appear as a construction or as a theorem discharging the
corresponding obligation.  If a theorem assumes the output of the repair instead
of constructing it, that theorem is conditional on the repair.

\paragraph{Obligation structure.}
An obligation structure is a record whose fields are the data and estimates
needed by a later construction.  This is acceptable only as an internal target
or as a hypothesis of a conditional helper.  Such a structure becomes statement
drift if it is added to a paper-facing theorem instead of being constructed
inside the proof.  The review question is whether every load-bearing field is
proved from the source hypotheses or is explicitly tracked as a missing
obligation.

\section{The main failure mode}

Suppose the paper proves
\[
  H \Longrightarrow C.
\]
During formalization, the proof may need an intermediate assertion \(B\).  The
paper theorem should be represented as
\[
  H \Longrightarrow B \Longrightarrow C
  \quad\text{inside the proof,}
\]
where \(B\) is obtained by a lemma or theorem from \(H\).  The following
public statement is a different theorem:
\[
  H \land B \Longrightarrow C.
\]
It is not unsound in \Lean{}, but it is not the paper theorem.  It says that the
conclusion follows if the missing bridge data is supplied.  Such a theorem is a
conditional helper, even if its conclusion looks exactly like the paper's
conclusion.

This is the situation colloquially described as ``adding a bridge
hypothesis''.  More precisely, an unproved intermediate step has been promoted
from the proof body to the theorem's assumptions.  The correction is not to hide
the hypothesis under a different structure name.  The correction is to keep a
paper-facing theorem with the source statement and move the missing step to a
named internal proof obligation.

\section{Faithful boundary hypotheses}

Not every extra formal hypothesis is a theorem drift.  Some hypotheses are
faithful boundary conditions introduced by formal encoding.  Examples include
nonnegativity needed for a real power, positivity needed to divide by a
quantity, finiteness and nonemptiness of an index type, a field-model instance,
or decidability instances required by \Lean{}.  Such hypotheses are acceptable
when they express part of the mathematical ambient setting or make explicit a
condition used implicitly in the paper.

The distinction is load-bearing.  A faithful boundary hypothesis describes the
domain in which the paper's objects live.  A proof-debt hypothesis supplies a
mathematical step that the proof should derive.  If removing the hypothesis
leaves an unproved construction or estimate from the paper proof, then the
hypothesis is proof debt, not a boundary condition.

\section{Definition drift and subtree repair}

Definition drift is especially dangerous because it propagates.  If a
definition is changed so that it no longer denotes the object in the paper,
then every downstream theorem using that definition may continue to compile
while proving statements about the wrong object.  Downstream theorem statements
can then be repaired piecemeal, but the development remains unstable because
the wrong definition is still upstream.

When a definition mismatch is found, the repair should proceed by a subtree
protocol.

\begin{enumerate}
  \item Identify the source object and the formal object precisely.
  \item Freeze a source-faithful definition or state an adapter theorem
  relating the existing definition to the source object.
  \item Recheck the downstream theorem chain against that definition or adapter.
  \item Re-formalize the affected subtree from the corrected interface, rather
  than adding local hypotheses to each downstream theorem.
  \item If a downstream proof cannot be completed, record the missing obligation
  at the lowest point where the paper proof needs it.
\end{enumerate}

This is slower than editing a final theorem signature, but it prevents a local
definition error from becoming a global theorem-statement error.

\section{Allowed shapes}

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{p{0.24\linewidth}p{0.31\linewidth}p{0.32\linewidth}}
\textbf{Shape} & \textbf{Allowed use} & \textbf{Forbidden use} \\
\hline
Paper-facing theorem & Matches the source statement up to faithful encoding &
Carries non-paper bridge, residual, repair, input, obligation-structure, or
proof-obligation hypotheses \\
Source-shaped theorem with a tracked \verb|sorry| & Default repair when the
source proof is blocked but the statement is known & Replaced by a strengthened
theorem statement merely to keep the file compiling \\
Conditional helper & Temporary quarantine for substantial proof content whose
remaining named obligation has not yet been discharged & Introduced merely to
avoid a \verb|sorry|, or linked as the source theorem or marked as
proof-complete for that theorem \\
Obligation discharger theorem & Constructs the obligation from paper hypotheses &
Merely restates the obligation as an assumption \\
Input bundle & Collects produced data for a local construction & Is assumed by a
source theorem instead of being produced \\
Obligation structure & Bundles constructed data and estimates & Hides unproved

When a source-labelled proof is blocked, use the following order.

\begin{enumerate}

  \path{references/ldt-paper/}.
  \item Write the paper theorem form, the current \Lean{} theorem form, and the
  first missing intermediate assertion.
  \item Decide whether the missing assertion is a faithful boundary condition,
  a representation adapter, an ordinary lemma from the paper proof, or a real
  paper-gap discrepancy.
  \item If it is an ordinary lemma or adapter, create a named theorem which
  discharges that obligation.  Do not add it to the source theorem as a new
  hypothesis.
  \item Keep the source-labelled theorem itself in the source form, even if its
  proof must contain a tracked \verb|sorry|.  This is the default repair when
  the missing assertion has not yet been proved.
  \item Create a conditional helper only to quarantine substantial proof content
  that already exists and would otherwise be lost.  Do not create such a helper
  merely to avoid a \verb|sorry| or to keep making progress.  If a conditional
  helper remains, give it a conditional name, keep it separate from the
  paper-facing theorem, and record the obligation discharger that must eliminate
  it.
  \item If the source and formal statements genuinely differ, write or update a
  note under \path{docs/paper-gaps/} before marking the statement as aligned.
  \item Update the blueprint so that paper labels point only to paper-facing
  declarations.  Conditional helpers belong in remarks or implementation

\end{enumerate}
